verses.zh: 「你们存活于世的日子，在耶和华―你们列祖的　神所赐你们为业的地上，要谨守遵行的律例典章乃是这些：
verses.en: These are the statutes and ordinances you must be careful to obey as long as you live in the land the Lord, the God of your ancestors,[NOTE:1] has given you to possess.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “fathers.”

Heb “you must be careful to obey in the land the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you to possess all the days which you live in the land.” This adverbial statement modifies “to obey,” not “to possess,” so the order in the translation has been rearranged to make this clear.

verses.zh: 你们要将所赶出的国民事奉神的各地方，无论是在高山，在小山，在各青翠树下，都毁坏了；
verses.en: You must by all means destroy[NOTE:1] all the places where the nations you are about to dispossess worship their gods—on the high mountains and hills and under every leafy tree.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “destroying you must destroy”; KJV “Ye shall utterly (surely ASV) destroy”; NRSV “must demolish completely.” The Hebrew infinitive absolute precedes the verb for emphasis, which is reflected in the translation by the words “by all means.”

Every leafy tree. This expression refers to evergreens which because they keep their foliage throughout the year, provided apt symbolism for nature cults such as those practiced in Canaan. The deity particularly in view is Asherah, wife of the great god El, who was considered the goddess of fertility and whose worship frequently took place at shrines near or among clusters (groves) of such trees (see also Deut 7:5). See J. Hadley, NIDOTTE 1:569-70; J. DeMoor, TDOT 1:438-44.

verses.zh: 也要拆毁他们的祭坛，打碎他们的柱像，用火焚烧他们的木偶，砍下他们雕刻的神像，并将其名从那地方除灭。
verses.en: You must tear down their altars, shatter their sacred pillars,[NOTE:1] burn up their sacred Asherah poles,[NOTE:2] and cut down the images of their gods; you must eliminate their very memory from that place.
notes: Sacred pillars. These are the stelae (stone pillars; the Hebrew term is מַצֵּבֹת, matsevot) associated with Baal worship, perhaps to mark a spot hallowed by an alleged visitation of the gods. See also Deut 7:5.
Sacred Asherah poles. The Hebrew term (plural) is אֲשֵׁרִים (ʾasherim). See note on the word “(leafy) tree” in v. 2, and also Deut 7:5.

verses.zh: 你们不可照他们那样事奉耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: You must not worship the Lord your God the way they worship.

verses.zh: 但耶和华―你们的　神从你们各支派中选择何处为立他名的居所，你们就当往那里去求问，
verses.en: But you must seek only the place he[NOTE:1] chooses from all your tribes to establish his name as his place of residence,[NOTE:2] and you must go there.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.

Some scholars, on the basis of v. 11, emend the MT reading שִׁכְנוֹ (shikhno, “his residence”) to the infinitive construct לְשַׁכֵּן (leshakken, “to make [his name] to dwell”), perhaps with the third person masculine singular sf לְשַׁכְּנוֹ (leshakkeno, “to cause it to dwell”). Though the presupposed noun שֵׁכֶן (shekhen) is nowhere else attested, the parallel here with שַׁמָּה (shammah, “there”) favors retaining the MT as it stands.

verses.zh: 将你们的燔祭、平安祭、十分取一之物，和手中的举祭，并还愿祭、甘心祭，以及牛群羊群中头生的，都奉到那里。
verses.en: And there you must take your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, the personal offerings you have prepared,[NOTE:1] your votive offerings, your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks.
notes: Heb “heave offerings of your hand.”

verses.zh: 在那里，耶和华―你们　神的面前，你们和你们的家属都可以吃，并且因你手所办的一切事蒙耶和华―你的　神赐福，就都欢乐。
verses.en: Both you and your families[NOTE:1] must feast there before the Lord your God and rejoice in all the output of your labor with which he[NOTE:2] has blessed you.
notes: Heb “and your houses,” referring to entire households. The pronouns “you” and “your” are plural in the Hebrew text.
Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 12:5.

verses.zh: 我们今日在这里所行的是各人行自己眼中看为正的事，你们将来不可这样行；
verses.en: You must not do as we are doing here today, with everyone[NOTE:1] doing what seems best to him,
notes: Heb “a man.”

verses.zh: 因为你们还没有到耶和华―你　神所赐你的安息地，所给你的产业。
verses.en: for you have not yet come to the final stop[NOTE:1] and inheritance the Lord your God is giving you.
notes: Heb “rest.”

verses.zh: 但你们过了约旦河，得以住在耶和华―你们　神使你们承受为业之地，又使你们太平，不被四围的一切仇敌扰乱，安然居住。
verses.en: When you do go across the Jordan River[NOTE:1] and settle in the land he[NOTE:2] is granting you as an inheritance and you find relief from all the enemies who surround you, you will live in safety.[NOTE:3]
notes: The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 12:5.
In the Hebrew text vv. 10-11 are one long, complex sentence. For stylistic reasons the translation divides this into two sentences.

verses.zh: 那时要将我所吩咐你们的燔祭、平安祭、十分取一之物，和手中的举祭，并向耶和华许愿献的一切美祭，都奉到耶和华―你们　神所选择要立为他名的居所。
verses.en: Then you must come to the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to reside, bringing[NOTE:1] everything I am commanding you—your burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, the personal offerings you have prepared,[NOTE:2] and all your choice votive offerings that you devote to him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and it will be (to) the place where the Lord your God chooses to cause his name to dwell you will bring.”
Heb “heave offerings of your hand.”
Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 12:5.

verses.zh: 你们和儿女、仆婢，并住在你们城里无分无业的利未人，都要在耶和华―你们的　神面前欢乐。
verses.en: You shall rejoice in the presence of the Lord your God, along with your sons, daughters, male and female servants, and the Levites in your villages[NOTE:1] (since they have no allotment or inheritance with you).[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “within your gates” (so KJV, NASB); NAB “who belongs to your community.”
They have no allotment or inheritance with you. See note on the word “inheritance” in Deut 10:9.

verses.zh: 你要谨慎，不可在你所看中的各处献燔祭。
verses.en: Make sure you do not offer burnt offerings in any place you wish,

verses.zh: 惟独耶和华从你那一支派中所选择的地方，你就要在那里献燔祭，行我一切所吩咐你的。
verses.en: for you may do so[NOTE:1] only in the place the Lord chooses in one of your tribal areas—there you may do everything I am commanding you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “offer burnt offerings.” The expression “do so” has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.

This injunction to worship in a single and central sanctuary—one limited and appropriate to the thrice-annual festival celebrations (see Exod 23:14-17; 34:22-24; Lev 23:4-36; Deut 16:16-17)—marks a departure from previous times when worship was carried out at local shrines (cf. Gen 8:20; 12:7; 13:18; 22:9; 26:25; 35:1, 3, 7; Exod 17:15). Apart from the corporate worship of the whole theocratic community, however, worship at local altars would still be permitted as in the past (Deut 16:21; Judg 6:24-27; 13:19-20; 1 Sam 7:17; 10:5, 13; 2 Sam 24:18-25; 1 Kgs 18:30).

verses.zh: 「然而，在你各城里都可以照耶和华―你　神所赐你的福分，随心所欲宰牲吃肉；无论洁净人不洁净人都可以吃，就如吃羚羊与鹿一般。
verses.en: On the other hand, you may slaughter and eat meat as you please when the Lord your God blesses you[NOTE:1] in all your villages.[NOTE:2] Both the ritually pure and impure may eat it, whether it is a gazelle or an ibex.
notes: Heb “only in all the desire of your soul you may sacrifice and eat flesh according to the blessing of the Lord your God which he has given to you.”
Heb “gates” (so KJV, NASB; likewise in vv. 17, 18).

verses.zh: 只是不可吃血，要倒在地上，如同倒水一样。
verses.en: However, you must not eat blood—pour it out on the ground like water.

verses.zh: 你的五谷、新酒，和油的十分之一，或是牛群羊群中头生的，或是你许愿献的，甘心献的，或是手中的举祭，都不可在你城里吃。
verses.en: You will not be allowed to eat in your villages your tithe of grain, new wine, olive oil, the firstborn of your herd and flock, any votive offerings you have vowed, or your freewill and personal offerings.

verses.zh: 但要在耶和华―你的　神面前吃，在耶和华―你　神所要选择的地方，你和儿女、仆婢，并住在你城里的利未人，都可以吃；也要因你手所办的，在耶和华―你　神面前欢乐。
verses.en: Only in the presence of the Lord your God may you eat these, in the place he[NOTE:1] chooses. This applies to you, your son, your daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levites[NOTE:2] in your villages. In that place you will rejoice before the Lord your God in all the output of your labor.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 12:5.
See note at Deut 12:12.
Heb “in all the sending forth of your hands.”

verses.zh: 你要谨慎，在你所住的地方永不可丢弃利未人。
verses.en: Be careful not to overlook the Levites as long as you live in the land.

verses.zh: 「耶和华―你的　神照他所应许扩张你境界的时候，你心里想要吃肉，说：『我要吃肉』，就可以随心所欲地吃肉。
verses.en: When the Lord your God extends your borders as he said he would do and you say, “I want to eat meat just as I please,”[NOTE:1] you may do so as you wish.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for my soul desires to eat meat.”
Heb “according to all the desire of your soul you may eat meat.”

verses.zh: 耶和华―你　神所选择要立他名的地方若离你太远，就可以照我所吩咐的，将耶和华赐给你的牛羊取些宰了，可以随心所欲在你城里吃。
verses.en: If the place he[NOTE:1] chooses to locate his name is too far for you, you may slaughter any of your herd and flock he[NOTE:2] has given you just as I have stipulated; you may eat them in your villages[NOTE:3] just as you wish.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 12:5.
Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 12:5.
Heb “gates” (so KJV, NASB); NAB “in your own community.”

verses.zh: 你吃那肉，要像吃羚羊与鹿一般；无论洁净人不洁净人都可以吃。
verses.en: As you eat the gazelle or ibex, so you may eat these; the ritually impure and pure alike may eat them.

verses.zh: 只是你要心意坚定，不可吃血，因为血是生命；不可将血（原文是生命）与肉同吃。
verses.en: However, by no means eat the blood, for the blood is life itself[NOTE:1]—you must not eat the life with the meat.
notes: The blood is life itself. This is a figure of speech (metonymy) in which the cause or means (the blood) stands for the result or effect (life). That is, life depends upon the existence and circulation of blood, a truth known empirically but not scientifically tested and proved until the 17th century a.d. (cf. Lev 17:11).

verses.zh: 不可吃血，要倒在地上，如同倒水一样。
verses.en: You must not eat it! You must pour it out on the ground like water.

verses.zh: 不可吃血。这样，你行耶和华眼中看为正的事，你和你的子孙就可以得福。
verses.en: You must not eat it so that it may go well with you and your children after you; you will be doing what is right in the Lord’s sight.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in the eyes of the Lord.” The LXX adds “your God” to create the common formula, “the Lord your God.” The MT is preferred precisely because it does not include the stereotyped formula; thus it more likely preserves the original text.

verses.zh: 只是你分别为圣的物和你的还愿祭要奉到耶和华所选择的地方去。
verses.en: But the holy things and votive offerings that belong to you, you must pick up and take to the place the Lord will choose.[NOTE:1]
notes: Again, to complete a commonly attested wording the LXX adds after “choose” the phrase “to place his name there.” This shows insensitivity to deliberate departures from literary stereotypes. The MT reading is to be preferred.

verses.zh: 你的燔祭，连肉带血，都要献在耶和华―你　神的坛上。平安祭的血要倒在耶和华―你　神的坛上；平安祭的肉，你自己可以吃。
verses.en: You must offer your burnt offerings, both meat and blood, on the altar of the Lord your God; the blood of your other sacrifices[NOTE:1] you must pour out on his[NOTE:2] altar while you eat the meat.
notes: These other sacrifices would be so-called peace or fellowship offerings whose ritual required a different use of the blood from that of burnt (sin and trespass) offerings (cf. Lev 3; 7:11-14, 19-21).
Heb “on the altar of the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.

verses.zh: 你要谨守听从我所吩咐的一切话，行耶和华―你　神眼中看为善，看为正的事。这样，你和你的子孙就可以永远享福。」
verses.en: Pay careful attention to all these things I am commanding you so that it may always go well with you and your children after you when you do what is good and right in the sight of the Lord your God.

verses.zh: 「耶和华―你　神将你要去赶出的国民从你面前剪除，你得了他们的地居住，
verses.en: When the Lord your God eliminates the nations from the place where you are headed and you dispossess them, you will settle down in their land.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “dwell in their land” (so NASB). In the Hebrew text vv. 29-30 are one long sentence. For stylistic reasons the translation divides it into two.

verses.zh: 那时就要谨慎，不可在他们除灭之后随从他们的恶俗，陷入网罗，也不可访问他们的神说：『这些国民怎样事奉他们的神，我也要照样行。』
verses.en: After they have been destroyed from your presence, be careful not to be ensnared like they are; do not pursue their gods and say, “How do these nations serve their gods? I will do the same.”

verses.zh: 你不可向耶和华―你的　神这样行，因为他们向他们的神行了耶和华所憎嫌所恨恶的一切事，甚至将自己的儿女用火焚烧，献与他们的神。
verses.en: You must not worship the Lord your God the way they do![NOTE:1] For everything that is abhorrent[NOTE:2] to him,[NOTE:3] everything he hates, they have done when worshiping their gods. They even burn up their sons and daughters before their gods!
notes: Heb “you must not do thus to/for the Lord your God.”
See note on this term at Deut 7:25.
Heb “every abomination of the Lord.” See note on the word “his” in v. 27.

verses.zh: 凡我所吩咐的，你们都要谨守遵行，不可加添，也不可删减。
verses.en: (13:1)[NOTE:1] You[NOTE:2] must be careful to do everything I am commanding you. Do not add to it or subtract from it![NOTE:3]
notes: Beginning with 12:32, the verse numbers through 13:18 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 12:32 ET = 13:1 HT, 13:1 ET = 13:2 HT, 13:2 ET = 13:3 HT, etc., through 13:18 ET = 13:19 HT. With 14:1 the verse numbers in the ET and HT are again the same.

This verse highlights a phenomenon found throughout Deuteronomy, but most especially in chap. 12, namely, the alternation of grammatical singular and plural forms of the pronoun (known as Numeruswechsel in German scholarship). Critical scholarship in general resolves the “problem” by suggesting varying literary traditions—one favorable to the singular pronoun and the other to the plural—which appear in the (obviously rough) redacted text at hand. Even the ancient versions were troubled by the lack of harmony of grammatical number and in this verse, for example, offered a number of alternate readings. The MT reads “Everything I am commanding you (plural) you (plural) must be careful to do; you (singular) must not add to it nor should you (singular) subtract form it.” Smr, LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate suggest singular for the first two pronouns but a few Smr mss propose plural for the last two. What both ancient and modern scholars tend to overlook, however, is the covenantal theological tone of the Book of Deuteronomy, one that views Israel as a collective body (singular) made up of many individuals (plural). See M. Weinfeld, Deuteronomy 1-11 (AB), 15-16; J. A. Thompson, Deuteronomy (TOTC), 21-23.

Do not add to it or subtract from it. This prohibition makes at least two profound theological points: (1) This work by Moses is of divine origination (i.e., it is inspired) and therefore can tolerate no human alteration; and (2) the work is complete as it stands (i.e., it is canonical).

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This starts the amplification of the Ten Words into daily regulations (i.e. Deuteronomy 12-26), which cover
Israel's secular and sacred life. If one follows the outline of the Hittite Treaties, then (1) 4:1-11:32 contains the
foundational laws and (2) Deut. 12:1-26:19 is the characteristic expansion and explanation of those laws.
Scholars have delineated four "Law Codes" in the Pentateuch:

- Book of the covenant, Exod. 20:22-23:33

- Priestly Code, Exodus 25-31 and 34:29 through Leviticus 16

- Holiness Code, Leviticus 17-26

- Deuteronomic Code, Deut. 12-26 and 28

However, this listing is more effected by Julius Wellhausen's source critical
approach (i.e. J=YHWH; E=Elohim; D=Deuteronomy; and P=priestly writers) to the Pentateuch
than contemporary, second millennium B.C. parallels (cf. R. K. Harrison, Old
Testament times and John H. Walton, Ancient Israelite Literature In Its Cultural Context).

- This is the chapter where the controversy concerning the date of Deuteronomy rages. It centers around
Deut. 12:1-7 which call for one central worship altar (later Jerusalem).

- It seems that this text relates to two separate periods and purposes: (1) in the wilderness (i.e. tabernacle)
and (2) in the Promised Land. The purpose of all laws is proper worship of YHWH in place, motive and form.
Idolatry and its worship sites are rejected. The tension seems to be between legitimate local places of worship
(Exod. 20:24; Deut. 16:21) and a central place of Israeli worship. Local and special altars (cf. Deuteronomy 27) were
allowed (e.g. 1 Kgs. 3:3-5), but the Ark, tabernacle, and later the temple are emphasized (i.e. one central cultic site).

- Historically it is to be noted that Hezekiah's reform was more oriented toward a central worship site than was
Josiah's reform, which is usually used as the supposed historical occasion for the writing of Deuteronomy
(i.e. 621 B.C., cf. 2 Kgs. 18:22; 2 Chr. 32:12 and Isa. 36:7). Josiah's reform primarily dealt with
idolatry not centralized worship! I personally reject the JEDP theory of Pentateuch source criticism (cf. Josh
McDowell More Evidence That Demands A Verdict).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 12:1-7

1"These are the statutes and the judgments which you shall carefully
observe in the land which the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you to possess as long as you
live on the earth. 2You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations whom you shall dispossess serve their gods,
on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree. 3You shall tear down their altars and smash their sacred
pillars and burn their Asherim with fire, and you shall cut down the engraved images of their gods and obliterate their name from that place.
4You shall not act like this toward the Lord your God. 5But you shall seek the
Lord at the place which the Lord your God will choose from all your tribes,
to establish His name there for His dwelling, and there you shall come. 6There you shall bring your burnt offerings, your sacrifices,
your tithes, the contribution of your hand, your votive offerings, your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock. 7There
also you and your households shall eat before the Lord your God, and rejoice in all your undertakings in which the Lord your God has blessed you."

12:1 "the statutes and judgments" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "you shall carefully observe" This is a combination of a VERB, "keep watch" (BDB 1036,
KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT) and a Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, (BDB 793,
KB 889). This is a recurrent theme (e.g. Exod. 23:13,21; 34:11-12; Lev. 18:4-5,26,30; Deut. 4:6,9,15,23,40; and many more
especially in Deuteronomy and Wisdom Literature).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "which the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you" The VERB
shows completed action (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PERFECT), yet the events are future. It is a Hebrew way of
showing certainty (i.e. PROPHETIC PERFECT). This is a recurrent theme in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 1:8,20,21,25,35,36,39;
2:29; 3:18,20; 4:1,21,38,40; 5:16,31; 6:10,23; 7:13,16; 8:10; 9:6,23; 10:11; 11:9,17,21,31; 12:1,9; 15:4; 17:14; 18:9; 19:1,2,8,14; 21:23;
24:4; 25:15,19; 26:1,2,3,6,9,10,15; 27:3; 28:8,11,52; 31:7; 32:49; 34:4). It shows YHWH's gracious choice and provision for Israel.

▣ "to possess" The VERB (BDB 439, KB 441, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) is a
recurrent promise.

SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

▣ "on the earth" "On the earth" is another way of saying "in the Land" (cf. Deut. 12:19). As long as the
Israelites kept God's commandments, they could live in the Promised Land. See note at Deut. 4:40.

This verse has two different words for "land":

- "in the land" ‒ BDB 75

- "on the earth" ‒ BDB 9

They both refer to the whole earth or to the land of Canaan. They are usually synonyms
(cf. Deut. 4:38-40; 11:8-9; 12:1; 26:2,15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH

SPECIAL TOPIC: WORLD (several terms)

12:2 "utterly destroy all the places" "Utterly destroy" comes from a Hebrew word that means "cause to perish"
(BDB 1, KB 2, Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Piel IMPERFECT VERB, which
show intensity, cf. Deut. 12:3; Num. 33:52 [twice]; 2 Kgs. 21:3). YHWH was admonishing the Israelites to destroy the
pagan altars so as not to become a part of their fertility worship (cf. Exod. 23:24; 34:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: UTTERLY DESTROY

▣ "on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree" These are the locations of local
Ba'al and Asherah altars where fertility rites were practiced (cf. Jer. 2:20; 3:2,6; 17:2; Isa. 57:5,7; Hosea 4:13).

12:3 "their altars. . .sacred pillars. . .Asherim" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL'S MANDATED RESPONSE TO CANAANITE FERTILITY WORSHIP

▣ "you shall obliterate their name from this place" The VERB (BDB 1, KB, 2; Piel PERFECT
with waw) means "destroy." It is used several times in this context (i.e. Deut. 11:4,17; 12:2 [twice], 3).

YHWH's name is to be "established" (BDB 1014, KB 1496, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT),
but Ba'al and Asherah destroyed!

Israel either destroys the pagan idols or she will be destroyed by YHWH (i.e. Deut. 8:19,20; 11:17; 28:15-19, 63).
This reflects the "two ways" (i.e. blessings or cursings, your choice confirmed by your actions, cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30;
Psalm 1).

12:5 "the place which the Lord your God shall choose" God chose (BDB 103,
KB 119, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 12:11,14,18,21,26; 14:23-25; 15:20; 16:2,6,11,15; 17:8,10; 18:6; 26:2; 31:11)
the worship site (cf. Exod. 20:24).

The tabernacle (ark) traveled with Israel:

- Gilgal, Josh. 4:19; 10:6,15

- Shechem, Josh. 8:33

- Shiloh, Josh 18:1; Jdgs. 18:31; 1 Sam. 1:3

- Bethel, (possible) Jdg. 20:18,26-28; 21:2

- Kiriath-jearim, ark, 1 Sam. 6:21; 7:1-2 (priests at Nob, cf. 1 Samuel 21-22)

- Jerusalem

- David captures the citadel of Jebus (cf. 2 Sam. 5:1-10)

- David brings the ark to Jerusalem (cf. 2 Samuel 6)

- David purchases the site of the temple (2 Sam. 24:15-25; 2 Chr. 3:1)

Many modern scholars have tried to assert that Deuteronomy was written late to accommodate
Hezekiah and Josiah's reforms of centralizing Israel's worship. However, Deuteronomy does not name Jerusalem
as the specific site that YHWH will choose. In context the theological contrast is between:

- the local Ba'al shrines and the one shrine of Israel

- the monotheism of Israel versus the polytheism of Canaan (and the rest of the Ancient Near East)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

12:6 This verse lists several kinds of offerings:

- "burnt offerings" This meant wholly burnt offerings (BDB 750 II; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERINGS). This was a way of showing total,
complete dedication to God. It was a voluntary sacrifice (cf. Leviticus 1).

- "sacrifices" This refers to partially burnt, partially consumed offering (BDB 257). These were sin
offerings, peace offerings, thanksgiving offerings, etc. These were any offerings which had blood involved
(cf. Leviticus 7; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN OFFERING).

- "tithes" The tithe was Israel's way of supporting the priests, who were given no land inheritance
(see SPECIAL TOPIC: TITHING IN THE MOSAIC LEGISLATION).
There seem to be three tithes (BDB 798):

- for the central sanctuary

- for the local Levites, with the possibility of "a"

- every three years for the local poor (Lev. 27:30-33; Num. 18:21-22)

- "contributions of your hand" This is the Hebrew word for "heave-offerings" (BDB 929, cf. Lev. 7:32). This
refers to a sacrifice where some part of the animal is lifted off for the priests to eat.

- "votive offerings" This (BDB 623) is an example of a conditional vow to YHWH, "I'll do this, if You will do
that." This is the Jews keeping their part of the vow (Lev. 7:16-18).

- "freewill offerings" This (BDB 621) refers to an offering in thanks or praise from one who was
overwhelmed with the goodness of YHWH (cf. Lev. 22:18ff).

- "first-born" This (BDB 114) is a reference to the Death Angel going through Egypt killing the firstborn
of cattle and mankind. In light of this event all the first born of cattle and humans belonged uniquely to YHWH
(cf. Exod.13; Lev. 27:26-27)!

12:7 "you and your household shall eat before the Lord" This refers to a
fellowship meal, which is a theological precursor of both Passover and Eucharist (cf. Deut. 12:12,18; 14:26; Rev. 3:20).
YHWH's people were created to rejoice (BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal PERFECT with waw) with Him
in the physicalness of creation and the intimacy of worship (cf. Lev. 23:40; Num. 10:10; Deut. 12:7,12,18; 14:26; 16:11; 26:11; 27:7; 28:47).

8"You shall not do at all what we are doing here today, every man doing
whatever is right in his own eyes; 9for you have not as yet come to the resting place and the inheritance which the Lord
your God is giving you. 10When you cross the Jordan and live in the land which the Lord your God is giving
you to inherit, and He gives you rest from all your enemies around you so that you live in security, 11then it shall come about that the

and the Levite who is within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance with you."

12:8 "You shall not do at all what we are doing here today" Things will be more uniform in the Promised Land. The
religious practices during the wilderness wanderings period were simpler than the more organized practices in the
Promised Land and, especially at the temple, later located in Jerusalem.

▣ "every man doing whatever is right in his own eyes" This phrase has a neutral connotation
here, but in Judges it takes on a sinister connotation of an individual asserting freedom from covenant obligations
either through sinful choice or covenant ignorance (cf. Deut. 17:6; 21:25).

12:9 See note at Deut. 12:1

12:10 "He gives you rest. . .security" YHWH gives you rest (BDB 628, KB 679, Hiphil PERFECT
with waw) from your enemies. This security (BDB 442, KB 444, Qal PERFECT with waw) was
not achieved because of Israel's great military might, but because of the presence of YHWH.

12:11 "the place in which the Lord your God shall choose" This is a reference to
the centralized place of worship (i.e. the tabernacle and the ark, cf. Deut. 12:5,14), which was first at Shiloh.
See full note at Deut. 12:5.

12:12 "you shall rejoice" This is the purpose of YHWH's laws (cf. Deut. 12:7,18; 14:26; 28:47).

▣ "you and" Notice how everyone in the family including servants and the local Levites (cf. Deut. 12:19)
were to be included! In a sense these were all extended family members. They were loved and provided for, both in life's
necessities and for the next life (i.e. worship).

12:12, 19 "Levite who is within your gates" All priests were Levites, but not all Levites were priests. Here
"Levite" refers to the non-priests of the family of Levi who symbolized the poor and needy (cf. Deut. 12:18,19; 14:27,29;
16:11,14; 26:12-13), because the Levites had been given no land. They were respected local teachers of the Law.

made for YHWH (cf. Deut. 16:21; 1 Kgs. 3:4).

▣ "unclean and the clean" This does not refer to unclean animals as far as food (cf. Deut. 12:20-22; Leviticus 11),
but unclean animals as far as sacrifice. A blemished sheep could be eaten by humans as could some wild animals like
deer, but not pigs, etc.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOD LAWS (OT)

12:16 "you shall not eat the blood" This relates to the Hebrew reverence for blood as the symbol for life. Even
when they killed animals, whether for eating or sacrifice, they poured the blood out (cf. Deut. 15:23; Lev. 17:13) and
did not eat it, because life belonged to God. The blood represented life, life belongs to God (cf. Deut. 12:23-25;
Gen. 9:4; Lev. 7:11-12; 17:10-11,14)!

- "oil" ‒ BDB 850

This was an agricultural society.

12:32 "you shall not add nor take away from it" God is serious about obedience to His word (see note at Deut. 4:2). However,
Deuteronomy shows some adaptation of the laws of the desert period. We must apply the truths of the Bible for every new age
and culture. God revealed Himself to a particular culture at a particular time. Some of it is related only to that time and people
(e.g. holy war, polygamy, slavery, subjugation of women), but much of it is timeless truth to be applied to every age (for a
discussion of how to distinguish between the eternal and the cultural, see Fee and Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All
Its Worth, pp. 149-164 and Gordon Fee, Gospel and Spirit, pp. 1-36).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is there so much emphasis on a central worship site?

- Why did some of the laws change?

- Why is the blood so important to the Hebrews?

- Why are these rules so detailed?
